shared_elements: large elaborate headdress occupying upper third
arms held bent at the sides with hands near waist
horizontal banded elements across the waist/belt zone
tall upright stone slab/monolith format with rounded top
lower register/base with separate rectangular design blocks
justification: Both are tall upright stone monuments carrying a single frontal anthropomorphic figure organised in the same vertical sequence: broad ornamented headdress above, a prominent circular pectoral disc at the chest, arms bent inward at the sides, a banded belt or waist zone, and a distinct lower register at the base. The rendering differs sharply, however: A is coarse, dark, heavily weathered and carved almost in the round with soft swelling volumes, while B is a pale, crisply cut shallow relief on a flat slab, including neat rectangular glyph-like panels that have no counterpart in A.
